definition: Choreography means the art of designing and arranging movements for performers — dancers most of all, but also actors, marching bands, or anyone whose moves are planned step by step.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word choreography. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know choreography should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The heist film's most famous scene owes its tension to choreography: seven actors crossing a crowded casino floor on precisely timed paths.
Staging settles only the broad picture — where the set pieces sit and which side performers enter from; it stops far short of choreography, which designs every step they take.
Blocking maps actors' positions and crossings scene by scene, but it stops short of choreography, which fixes each movement to a count.

A routine is the finished sequence a performer learns and repeats — a floor routine, a tap routine. Choreography is the art of composing that sequence in the first place: the routine is the product, the choreography is the design behind it.

Orchestration is the arranging of music for an ensemble's instruments — and, figuratively, the behind-the-scenes coordination of any complex effort. Choreography composes the movement itself: who travels where, on which beat, one step at a time.

Choreography is more specific than 'planning' or 'staging': it names the art of designing the movements themselves — who travels where, on which beat — whether the movers are dancers, actors, or a marching band.
Choreography is the standard word wherever designed movement is the point — dance, stage combat, even camera work.

Watch a busy airport gate from the window and you are watching choreography, though nobody calls it that on the tarmac.
The plane noses in, and eight workers converge on marks they could find blindfolded.
The fuel truck arrives on one count, the baggage belt on another; the marshaller's wands carve the same arcs for every arrival.
None of this is improvised.
Every path is designed in advance, down to the step, so that no one crosses a spinning engine's line.
The designers who plan these movements study dance notation, one safety consultant admits, because nothing else records footwork so exactly.
